name: Queueing capacity planner
blurb: Requests at a rate, work that takes a while, and a target for how many may wait, at all or longer than a limit. Erlang C answers how many servers, shows what one fewer would cost, and draws the cliff.

inputs.label: Service time
inputs.description: Mean milliseconds of work per request. The mean, not the p99.

inputs.label: Target
inputs.description: The percentage of requests allowed to wait at all, or to wait longer than the wait limit when one is set.

inputs.label: Wait limit
inputs.description: 0 sizes for no wait at all. Set it to size for waits longer than this instead, such as 50 for a 50 ms queueing budget.

inputs.label: Check
inputs.description: Simulating runs a seeded Monte Carlo of the same queue, so the formula has something to disagree with.

inputs.label: Trials
inputs.description: Arrivals to simulate. Ignored unless simulating. The first tenth is discarded as warmup.
